concepts.def: The last Tsar of Russia, whose autocratic and incompetent rule from 1894 deepened social discontent and led to the fall of the Romanov dynasty.
Mass unrest sparked by Bloody Sunday and defeat by Japan, forcing Nicholas II to grant the October Manifesto and a Duma parliament.
Strikes and mutinies in Petrograd forced Nicholas II to abdicate, ending tsarism and creating a Provisional Government alongside the Soviets.
Lenin's Bolsheviks seized power from the Provisional Government in Petrograd, establishing the first communist state in Russia.
Conflict between the Bolshevik Reds and anti-Bolshevik Whites, won by the Reds, consolidating communist control across the former empire.
Lenin's partial return to market trade and private enterprise after War Communism, aimed at reviving the shattered Soviet economy.

Russia in Revolution 1894-1924 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Russia in Revolution 1894-1924 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Who was the last Tsar of Russia?
options: Nicholas II
Alexander III
Kerensky
Lenin

mcqs.q: What did the February Revolution of 1917 bring about?
options: The abdication of Nicholas II
The Bolsheviks taking power
The start of the NEP
Victory over Japan

mcqs.q: Who led the Bolsheviks to power in October 1917?
options: Lenin
Stalin
Trotsky alone
Kerensky

mcqs.q: What was the New Economic Policy of 1921?
options: A partial return to private trade
Total state control of all farms
A war against Germany
A new tsarist constitution

mcqs.q: What happened in the Russian Revolution of 1917?
options: The 1905 Revolution made Lenin ruler of Russia.
The Bolsheviks overthrew the Tsar in 1917.
There were two revolutions: February overthrew the Tsar and installed the Provisional Government; October saw the Bolsheviks seize power from that government.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the NEP in 1921?
options: War Communism had wrecked the economy and caused famine and revolt, so the NEP allowed limited private trade to aid recovery.
The 1905 Revolution made Lenin ruler of Russia.
The NEP was Lenin abandoning communism entirely.
The NEP was a tsarist reform.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.
It forced concessions like the Duma but did not overthrow the Tsar, who soon clawed back power, leaving grievances unresolved.
The 1905 Revolution ended tsarist rule.
The 1905 Revolution made Lenin ruler of Russia.
